sentences.text: Adult Luanchuanraptor are estimated to have been 1.1 to 1.8 meters long and weighed between 2.2 and 2.5 kilograms, though some estimates suggest a height of 0.60 meters and a weight of approximately 12 kilograms.
This genus is distinguished by a stiff tail tip, short tail vertebrae spines, connected front tail chevrons, and a large opening in the shoulder bone.
This genus represents the first dromaeosaurid discovered in Asia outside of northeastern China or the Gobi Desert.
Luanchuanraptor is known from a partial skeleton found in the Qiupa Formation of Henan, China, with the holotype specimen, cataloged as 41HIII-0100, described by Lü and colleagues in 2007.
The fossil remains include the skull roof, neck and back vertebrae, tail bones, ribs, shoulder girdle, leg bones, and hand claws.
Recent phylogenetic analyses classify Luanchuanraptor as a velociraptorine closely related to Adasaurus.

Luanchuanraptor lived during the Late Maastrichtian stage, approximately 72 to 66 million years ago, while other data place the species in the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, roughly 84 to 71 million years ago.
The habitat consisted of shallow lakes and braided delta rivers.
Some researchers have suggested Luanchuanraptor belongs to the subfamily Averaptora, though this view is not widely accepted.
